HC-MoE v9: Rank Robustness and the Five-Estimator Grid

The two P0 experiments from v8 — is the signal carried by outliers, and should GLM stay?
October 4, 2026 · v9
Abstract. v8 ended with two cheap experiments that could each have overturned its headline: recompute every correlation on ranks and with the extremes clipped, in case a few tokens were carrying the Pearson values; and drop the GLM null estimator, which accounted for most of the disagreement between estimators. Both ran, both had decision rules written in advance, and both rules are applied here. The signal is not an outlier artifact: clipping the top and bottom 1% of tokens leaves every tier-A correlation within 0.91–1.05× of its raw value. GLM is removed from the primary grid: its implementation extrapolates a Laplace tail, which gives extreme routing logits p-values orders of magnitude larger than the other five nulls; without it the estimator spread falls from 0.0252 to 0.0134, at the 0.0128 noise floor, and no family changes sign. The two rules interact once: dropping GLM promotes ERNIE/fineweb-edu to tier A, and its rank correlation is +0.001, so the rank rule sends it back. The tier-A list ends where v8 left it: 13 cells, the same 13. What ranks add is a difference of shape between families. Gemma's negative association is as strong on ranks as on raw values (8 of 9 benchmarks beyond the floor either way), so it runs through the bulk of tokens. Qwen's is not: Spearman keeps a median 0.71 of its Pearson value, and in 4 of the 8 benchmarks where Qwen's Pearson correlation clears the floor, the rank correlation does not. Qwen's best cells survive comfortably (lambada r = +0.131, Spearman +0.111), but its association with Intelligence Gain looks concentrated in the upper part of HC's range rather than spread across it — which would also explain why its top-decile lift runs 1.5× the linear formula. The next experiment maps that shape directly.

1. Research goals and where the study stands

The two primary questions

  1. Does HC track token difficulty? r(HC, CEbig) and r(HC, CEsmall), answered first.
  2. Does HC track Intelligence Gain? r(HC, IG), IG = CEsmall − CEbig.

Null estimator, HC variant, control, statistic and — new this cycle — the correlation measure itself (Pearson, Spearman, winsorised) are secondary axes: checks on those two answers.

What this drop changes

Both P0 experiments from v8 ran; both pre-registered rules are applied

Experiment 1, rank and heavy-tail robustness. Spearman and 1%- and 0.5%-winsorised Pearson beside the raw Pearson, for all 432 configurations, with the same passage bootstrap. Rule: a tier-A cell whose Spearman falls below half its Pearson value drops to B. Outcome: winsorising changes nothing that matters; ranks change some cells a great deal, almost all of them in Qwen.

Experiment 2, drop GLM. Re-grade on the five remaining estimators. Rule: if tier-A cells and family signs survive, GLM leaves the default design and becomes a sensitivity. Outcome: all 13 of v8's tier-A cells stay tier A, 1 is promoted, every family keeps its sign. From this report on, the primary grid is 5 estimators × 2 variants = 10 configurations per cell.

Applied together — which neither experiment's own summary did, because the rank experiment ran on the six-estimator list — the promoted cell, ERNIE/fineweb-edu, fails the rank rule (Spearman/Pearson = 0.02). The final count is 13 tier-A IG cells, identical to v8’s list.

GLM's null has the wrong tail for this purpose, and removing it brings the estimators into agreement

The Lindsey GLM in empirical_null_lindsey.py fits a Poisson GLM to histogram counts in the centre of each layer's logit distribution, and its default design is linear in |x − μ| — a Laplace shape. Extrapolated into the tail, a Laplace density decays exponentially where a Gaussian decays quadratically in the exponent. On one Gemma layer this gives a logit of 4.0 a p-value of 0.0117 under GLM and 9.8×10−9 under GMM. Higher Criticism is built from exactly those small p-values, so GLM compresses HC on the tokens where routing is most anomalous. That is why it sat -0.0165 below the other five in v8, in three of four families at once.

The pre-registered rule asked two things of a five-estimator grid: keep every tier-A cell, keep every family's sign. Both hold. Spread falls from 0.0252 to 0.0134 against a 0.0128 floor; Qwen's from 0.0320 to 0.0192, ERNIE's from 0.0266 to 0.0179, Gemma's from 0.0419 to 0.0296; Liquid, where GLM was never the outlier, is unchanged at 0.0149. Because GLM pulled every cell downward, Qwen rises (+0.0538 → +0.0579) and Gemma becomes slightly less negative (-0.0500 → -0.0449). Tier A goes 13 → 14, with ERNIE/fineweb-edu promoted.

Figure 3 — Mean IG correlation under each null estimator, GLM included (mandatory figure)

Pooled over families, so each bar sits inside the floor through cancellation. GLM, in grey, is the low outlier; the other five span 0.0134.

Figure 4 — Estimator spread by family, with and without GLM

The measured floor is 0.0128. Gemma is the only family still clearly above it, and less so on ranks — part of its estimator sensitivity is about how extreme the tail p-values get, the same mechanism as GLM's.

Figure 6 — Estimator effect within each family, GLM included

GLM, at the right, pulls Qwen, ERNIE and Gemma down together. Among the other five, StudentTSkewed is now the most deviant, mainly in Gemma.

Gemma, per benchmark. Without GLM, Gemma's estimators still disagree by 0.017–0.050 within a benchmark, mostly between GMM (least negative) and StudentTSkewed (most negative). They agree on sign in 9 of 9 benchmarks; lambada is positive under all five. So Gemma's inversion is estimator-robust, and its size is uncertain by up to a factor of about two.

What dropping GLM does not establish. Five estimators agreeing does not make them right. The null's tail is extrapolated from the centre of the distribution in every method, and the true tail of the null cannot be read off data that contain anomalies. What the experiment shows is that GLM's divergence comes from one specific modelling choice, the Laplace shape, rather than from the Lindsey approach as such. The code already supports a Gaussian-decay GLM; running it is the cheap way to check that, and is proposed in section 16.

The tier-A list is not an outlier artifact

Clipping each variable at its 1st and 99th percentiles leaves every tier-A correlation within 0.91–1.05× of its raw value, and clipping at 0.5% gives the same picture. If a few extreme tokens were carrying the Pearson values, clipping them would have collapsed those cells. It does not touch them. The concern that has sat in this series' ‘not run’ column since v1 is closed in that form.

Ranks are harsher. Of the 14 Pearson tier-A cells on the primary grid, 11 are also tier A on Spearman. Under the pre-registered rule, only one falls below half: ERNIE/fineweb-edu, r = +0.0324 but Spearman +0.0006, which goes to B. It is the cell the GLM drop had just promoted, so the two rules leave the tier-A list exactly where v8 had it. Two more are flagged rank-sensitive — tier A on Pearson and under the rule, tier B on ranks: Gemma/competition_math (ratio 0.74), Liquid/tinystories (ratio 0.78).

Figure 7 — Pearson against Spearman, all 36 cells

Dashed grey: Spearman equals Pearson. Dotted amber: Spearman is half of Pearson, the rule's line. Gemma (green) and Liquid (purple) sit on the diagonal; Qwen (blue) falls toward the half line.

Figure 8 — The Pearson tier-A cells under three correlation measures

Winsorised (grey) tracks Pearson in every cell. Spearman (amber) mostly does too. The exceptions: ERNIE/fineweb-edu, where it collapses to zero; Qwen/fineweb-edu, where it roughly halves; and Gemma/competition_math and Liquid/tinystories, which lose about a quarter.

Gemma's association runs through all the tokens; Qwen's looks concentrated in HC's upper range

Across cells with |r| > 0.03, the median Spearman/Pearson ratio is 0.93 in Gemma, 0.92 in Liquid, 0.81 in ERNIE and 0.71 in Qwen. Gemma's negative association is beyond the floor in 8 of 9 benchmarks on Pearson and 8 of 9 on ranks; in structured-wikipedia and tinystories it is stronger on ranks. Qwen's positive association clears the floor in 8 of 9 benchmarks on Pearson and 4 on ranks: in hellaswag, pg19, structured-wikipedia, tinystories the rank correlation is near zero, and none is significantly negative.

Winsorising leaves those Qwen cells intact, so the difference is not a few extreme tokens. The most likely reading is a relationship that is flat through most of HC's range and rises in its upper part: Pearson weights that part by its magnitude, ranks do not. Two v8 observations fit the same shape — Qwen's empirical top-decile lift is 1.5× what a linear relationship predicts, and selecting on high IG inflated r rather than shrinking it. Ties in HC (many tokens at the same low value) could also lower Spearman. The binned HC–IG curve proposed in section 16 separates the two.

Figure 9 — Family means on both measures

Gemma's mean is the same on ranks. Qwen's drops by about a third.

A gap in the rule. v8's rule said what to do below 0.5 and above 0.8 but not between. Two cells sit there with a Spearman tier of B. They keep tier A here, as the rule's letter requires, and carry a rank-sensitive flag in every table. A reader who prefers the Spearman tier throughout gets 12 tier-A cells instead of 13.

Q1 — HC tracks token difficulty in every family, with a family-specific sign

Against CEbig: 31 of 36 cells outside the floor, 13 tier A. Against CEsmall: 28 of 36, 12 tier A. Qwen, ERNIE and Liquid are positive on both; Gemma is negative on both (-0.0284 p<0.01, -0.0472 p<0.01). Qwen's asymmetry, +0.0142 p<0.05 against the large model and +0.0556 p<0.01 against the small, is what produces its IG correlation.

Figure 10 — What HC tracks, by family

Family means over 90 configurations. Floor ±0.0128.

Q2 — HC tracks Intelligence Gain; 13 tier-A cells survive both rules

Mean |r| against IG 0.0460; 29 of 36 cells unanimous in sign across ten configurations. Final tiers: 13 A, 10 B, 13 C. By family: Qwen +0.0579 p<0.01, Gemma -0.0449 p<0.01, ERNIE +0.0047, Liquid +0.0052. ERNIE and Liquid average near zero through cancellation across benchmarks; each has tier-A cells of both signs.

Strongest cell: Qwen/lambada, r = +0.1307 (95% CI +0.1198–+0.1413), Spearman +0.1113, ESS 33,123, tolerating another 147× deflation, +0.23 sd of IG in the top HC decile by the linear formula (which understates it).

Figure 11 — The twelve strongest IG cells, both measures

Positive and negative extremes come from different families. Where amber falls short of blue, the cell's correlation lives in the upper range of HC.

IG is not yet separated from the difficulty gap. corr(rsmall − rbig, rIG) = 0.964. The defensible phrasing remains “HC predicts where the small model struggles more than the large one”.

Secondary axis: controls and statistic

On the primary grid Qwen keeps 69% of its IG correlation under the Fisher control and 82% under pmin; Gemma 45% and 76%. Across the 24 cells more than twice the floor, median retention is 56% (sign kept in 92%) and 77% (sign kept in 100%). InvMinP alone stays within ±0.008. The signal is multi-expert, and a little over half of it is distinct from a broad elevation of every p-value.

Figure 12 — What survives each control, by family

The two conditionings answer different questions and are never averaged. ERNIE and Liquid have no raw family-level effect to retain.

Consistent across variants: highest-to-lowest spread is only 0.0038 in r, well inside the 0.0128 noise floor. The conclusions do not depend on variant choice. On ranks the variant spread is 0.0005.

7. Compute ratio within Qwen (experiment 3, carried from v8)

Holding Qwen3-30B-A3B fixed and swapping the small partner between 0.6B (5.5×), 1.7B (1.9×) and 4B (0.8×). The experiment used GMM only, so the GLM decision does not touch it; it has not been re-run on ranks.

The gap scales the association but does not flip it

All tokens: +0.0641 at 5.5×, +0.0517 at 1.9×, +0.0280 at 0.8×; strictly ordered in 8 of 9 benchmarks, positive in all 9 at Gemma's gap. r(HC, CEbig) is constant (+0.0338); r(HC, CEsmall) carries the whole change. Gemma's inversion is not a small-gap effect.

Figure 13 — Qwen's association as the small partner grows

Means over nine benchmarks, all tokens. The flat CE_big line is the large model held fixed.

One open link to this cycle's result. If Qwen's association lives in HC's upper range, the compute-ratio question is better asked there too: does a larger small partner shrink the effect everywhere, or only among the most anomalous tokens? The binned-curve experiment in section 16 can be run on the three partners at no extra cost.

8. The IG-quantile slices (retired in v8)

Q50–Q95 keep tokens whose IG is at or above its Nth percentile. On identical tokens, that selection raised the HC–IG correlation in 27 of 27 experiment-3 cases (median ×1.9) and turned tinystories' +0.001 into +0.121. Experiment 1 showed the IG-selected values reproduce on held-out passages (r = +0.97), which is stability, not evidence of prediction. Nothing in this report uses them.

Figure 14 — Same tokens, two slices (Qwen, 0.6B partner)

Every top-quartile bar is taller. A relationship concentrated in the upper range of the joint distribution, as section 5 suggests for Qwen, makes this inflation larger.

14. Statistical health

CheckStatusResult
Grid completeness & numeric sanitydone432/432 cells, 0 duplicates, 0 unparsed columns. Avg_Inverse_Min_P still overflows (8.1e298) — descriptive only. The 26_08_30 full-network correlations and the 26_09_03 max_20pct correlations are identical in 1296/1296 rows (max difference 1e-16), so the two drops are joined exactly.
Monte-Carlo null reproductiondoneσ = 0.009866, crit_05 = 0.01934 reproduces — but it was computed at n = 10,000, which is the simulation size, not the sample size. Real n runs 12,314–477,782 (median 51,100). The iid floor is retired in favour of the measured one.
Empirical (Efron) nulldoneσ0 = 6.0 at measured ESS, 8.4 at true nominal n, 10.9 at the old n = 10,000 assumption. The residual is between-family heterogeneity, not a broken yardstick.
Block-bootstrap nulldonePassage-level bootstrap (1,000 resamples) on the full token set with the series' own statistic: 299/360 IG configurations exclude 0. Median deflation 2.61×. Both new experiments reuse the same passage bootstrap, so their CIs and grades are on the same footing.
Multiplicity / effective test countdone1.15 of 10 configurations per cell (mean pairwise r = 0.93); 360 configurations ≈ 41 independent tests.
BH false discovery ratedone292 of 360 full-network IG configurations at q < 0.05 on ESS-honest z. Permutation p-values are not used: 267/360 sit at the 1e-4 floor.
Autocorrelation robustness (ARF)doneGraded at each cell's own measured ESS. 14 of 36 full-network IG cells clear ARF ≥ 20 beyond their measured ESS.
Estimator consistencydoneResolved by a pre-registered decision. GLM removed from the primary grid (experiment 2): spread 0.0134 against the 0.0128 floor, down from 0.0252 with GLM; all original tier-A cells keep tier A and every family keeps its sign. Cause identified in the code: the Lindsey GLM extrapolates a Laplace tail, so extreme routing logits get far larger p-values. Residual per family: Qwen 0.0192, ERNIE 0.0179, Gemma 0.0296, Liquid 0.0149. Gemma's magnitudes still depend on the estimator; its signs do not.
HC variant consistencydonePass: spread 0.0038, inside the 0.0128 floor.
Control retention (Fisher, p_min)doneOn the five-estimator grid. Qwen retains 69% under Fisher and 82% under pmin; Gemma 45% and 76%. Across the 24 cells more than twice the floor, median retention is 56% (Fisher) and 77% (pmin). ERNIE and Liquid have no raw effect to retain.
Layer-subset selectiondoneSuperseded by a definition error. The ‘Q50–Q95 layer subsets’ are tokens whose Intelligence Gain is above its 50th–95th percentile (verified in the pipeline code and by an exact reproduction). Selecting on the outcome cannot support a claim that HC predicts it, so the selection question is moot: the primary slice is reset to the full token set.
Effect size (decile lift)doneFormula lift reported for every headline cell. E3 measured the lift empirically on the full token set; across 21 Qwen cells with |r| > 0.02 the empirical lift is 1.50× the 1.755·r formula (range -0.65–2.54). New in v9: the rank results explain why — Qwen's association is concentrated in the upper part of HC's range, which lifts the top decile above what a linear relationship predicts.
Difficulty-gap confoundpartialcorr(rsmall − rbig, rIG) = 0.964 at the full network. From E3: holding the large model fixed, r(HC, CEbig) is identical across all three small models while r(HC, CEsmall) falls as the small model grows — the IG association moves entirely through the small model. The token-level control has still not run.
Rank / heavy-tail robustnessdoneRun for the first time (experiment 1, on all 36 cells). 1%-winsorised Pearson keeps 0.91–1.05 of r in every tier-A cell, so a handful of extreme tokens is not the story. Spearman keeps a median 0.86; one tier-A cell (ERNIE/fineweb-edu, promoted by the GLM drop) falls below half and is demoted by the pre-registered rule. Qwen's ratio (0.71) is well below the other families'.
Sign-convention invariantdonePass everywhere: E1 0/11, E3 0/8, 26_09_03 max_20pct 0/35 testable rows inconsistent.
Statistic definition auditdoneThree corrections. (1) ‘Q75’ keeps 25.0% of tokens, chosen by IG ≥ its 75th percentile — selection on the outcome, not upper layers. (2) Max_Per_Row is max_20pct (identical in 432/432 cells). (3) The 26_08_30 drop is the full corpus, not a 10,000-token subsample.
Out-of-sample replicationdoneE1, pre-registered (GMM, standard, max_20pct, Q75): exploratory and held-out halves correlate +0.970 across 36 cells, 92% sign agreement, tier A 8→7. Replicates — but what replicates is an IG-selected quantity. The split is sequential, not random.

The same register as section 1.

15. Assessment

Holds up

  • HC tracks token difficulty in all four families; 31 and 28 of 36 cells outside the floor.
  • No outlier artifact: winsorising keeps 0.91–1.05 of r in every tier-A cell.
  • Qwen's four strong benchmarks: tier A on Pearson, Spearman and winsorised; lambada +0.131.
  • Gemma's inversion: every estimator, ranks, and the compute gap ruled out.
  • Estimator agreement after a pre-registered GLM decision with an identified cause; spread 0.0134.
  • The signal is multi-expert: 77% retention under pmin.

Not yet established

  • Qwen's weaker benchmarks (hellaswag, pg19, structured-wikipedia, tinystories): positive on Pearson, flat on ranks.
  • “Where scale helps”: corr(gap, IG) = 0.96; still the difficulty gap.
  • Gemma's magnitude: estimator spread 0.0296, up to a factor of two between GMM and StudentTSkewed.
  • The shape claim rests on a ratio; it has not been looked at directly.
  • Out-of-sample: the primary grid has never been split into held-out halves.

Open

  • What shape is the HC–IG relationship? Flat then rising, or linear with ties in HC?
  • Is GLM's problem the Laplace shape or the Lindsey method? A Gaussian-decay GLM answers it.
  • What inverts Gemma? Shared expert or per-layer embeddings.
  • Does HC predict IG beyond token difficulty? The token-level control.
  • Do the tier-A cells reproduce on random held-out passages?

v8 experimentStatusOutcome

Proposed

The shape of the HC–IG relationship

P0 · a few hours, existing token series
Question
Is Qwen's association concentrated in HC's upper range (rank ratio 0.71), or is the Spearman shortfall an artifact of ties in HC? This decides whether the practical design is a threshold on HC or a linear score.
Design
For every tier-A cell plus Qwen's rank-fragile benchmarks, GMM/standard: 20 equal-count bins of HC, mean IG per bin with passage-bootstrap bands. Also r(HC, IG) within HC ≥ its 75th percentile and within the rest, and the share of the covariance contributed by the top HC quartile. Report the fraction of tied HC values. Gemma as the comparison family.
Statistic
Covariance share of the top HC quartile; r below and above Q75; tie fraction.
Decision rule
If the top quartile carries more than 70% of the covariance and r in the lower three quartiles is inside the floor, Qwen's finding is restated as a threshold effect and HC-thresholding becomes the default analysis. If the binned curve is close to linear and ties exceed 20%, the Spearman gap is a tie artifact and the Pearson grades stand without qualification.

GLM with Gaussian decay

P1 · under an hour; the option exists in the code
Question
Is GLM's divergence the Laplace tail, or something in the Lindsey Poisson-GLM approach itself?
Design
Re-run the null fits with fit_config={'type': 'gaussian'} and recompute HC on the full grid.
Statistic
Offset of GLM-Gaussian from the five-estimator mean; tier changes.
Decision rule
If GLM-Gaussian lands inside the five-estimator envelope, restore it as the sixth estimator. If it still deviates, drop the Lindsey GLM permanently and say why.

Split the full grid into held-out halves

P1 · ~half a day
Question
Do the 13 tier-A cells reproduce on passages they were not measured on?
Design
Experiment 1 (v8)'s protocol with no IG mask and a random passage split; Pearson and Spearman.
Statistic
Exploratory-vs-held-out correlation across cells; tier A on each half.
Decision rule
If held-out tier A is within about 3 of exploratory and cell correlations exceed 0.8, the results are confirmed out of sample. If tier A halves, the grid is overfitting passage selection.

Isolate Gemma's inversion

P1 · ~1 day, small-model forward passes
Question
Shared expert or the E2B partner's per-layer embeddings?
Design
Swap Gemma's small partner for a dense model of similar size without per-layer embeddings, large model fixed.
Statistic
Sign and size of r(HC, IG) and r(HC, CEsmall) on both measures.
Decision rule
If the inversion disappears, the per-layer embeddings cause it and it says nothing about routing. If it persists, the shared expert is the remaining candidate.

Token-level control for baseline difficulty

P1 · ~2 days
Question
corr(gap, IG) = 0.96, open since v4. Does HC predict IG beyond token difficulty?
Design
Within deciles of CEbig, r(HC, IG) on both measures; and partial r(HC, IG | CEbig) at token level. Qwen's tier-A cells first.
Statistic
Stratified r and its stability across deciles; partial against raw.
Decision rule
If the partial keeps 60% or more and strata agree, ‘where scale helps’ becomes defensible. Below 30%, the IG framing reduces to the difficulty gap.
